ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $OD$ bisects $\angle AOC$, and $OE$ bisects $\angle COB$. If $\angle AOD = 20^\circ$ and $\angle EOB = 40^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle AOB$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since OD bisects $\angle AOC$ and OE bisects $\angle COB$, \\
$\therefore \angle AOC = 2\angle AOD$ and $\angle COB = 2\angle EOB$, \\
Since $\angle AOD = 20^\circ$ and $\angle EOB = 40^\circ$. \\
$\therefore \angle AOC = 2 \times 20^\circ = 40^\circ$ and $\angle BOC = 2 \times 40^\circ = 80^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle AOB = \angle AOC + \angle BOC = 40^\circ + 80^\circ = \boxed{120^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, five rays are emitted from point O, and in the order from left to right, from above to the lower right, they are respectively OA, OD, OC, OE, OB; therefore, the order of the adjacent rays inside ∠AOB is OA-OD-OC-OE-OB. Reasoning: It is known that OD bisects ∠AOC, and ∠AOD = 20°, so ∠DOC = 20°. It is known that OE bisects ∠COB, and ∠EOB = 40°, so ∠COE = 40°. Thus ∠AOB is composed of four adjacent angles: ∠AOD, ∠DOC, ∠COE, ∠EOB, so ∠AOB = 20° + 20° + 40° + 40° = 120°.
